displayPattern: LED behind the blower-door view port on a York TG9S. Each flash is 1/3 second on and 1/3 second off, then a 2-second pause: 1 red flash
meaning: Flame was sensed when there was not a call for heat. The control turns on both the inducer motor and the supply air blower.
causes: A leaking or slow-closing gas valve
diySteps: If you smell gas, leave the building and call the gas supplier from outside. Do not reset the furnace to clear the smell
Technician: check for a leaking or slow-closing gas valve
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
proAdvice: Call a licensed HVAC technician. York's diagnostics say to check for a leaking or slow-closing gas valve, and the same section says never to bypass a safety control.
